scope: Connected USB-C board observations, serial boot and read-only flash checks. No electrical VBUS/VIN qualification.
sources_of_identity: Windows USB/serial enumeration, esptool5.1.2 and private serial capture

boards.serial_passive_115200_observation: No bytes during first15-second window; not proof of firmware failure
boards.read_460800: Failed packet transfer; no write requested
boards.backup_storage: Private local folder outside Git; includes whole flash, potentially credentials/NVS
boards.end_state: esptool requested hard reset after successful comparison; existing flash image not replaced

boards.identity_limit: Boot text only, with altered characters; exact chip and flash ID not established by esptool
boards.esptool_connection: Not established: automatic reset and subsequent no-reset attempts at115200/57600 failed or timed out
boards.manual_actions: User confirmed initial BOOT sequence, EN/RESET during capture and a later BOOT-held sequence. Retried immediately after receiving the last confirmation.
boards.end_instruction: Release BOOT and press EN/RESET once to resume normal boot; no further programming attempted

last_confirmed_BOOT_attempt.reported_error: Serial data stream stopped: Possible serial noise or corruption.

platform_implications: User-confirmed25.4mm row spacing is retained for the measured board.
These CP210x observations do not identify either card as the advertised diymore CH340 variant or validate its30-pin map.
Same USB-C connector and row spacing do not establish the same VBUS/VIN power circuit.
Do not replace firmware to infer power-path behavior; follow manufacturing/usb_service_test.md on each identified board.
